facts.statement: The genus Pabwehshi was named in 2001 by Jeffrey A. Wilson and his colleagues.
facts.quote: Pabwehshi was named in 2001 by Jeffrey A. Wilson and colleagues.

facts.statement: Fossils of Pabwehshi were discovered in the Vitakri and Pab formations in Balochistan, Pakistan.
facts.quote: These specimens were found in Maastrichtian-age Upper Cretaceous rocks of the Vitakri and Pab formations in Balochistan, Pakistan

facts.statement: Pabwehshi lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: These specimens were found in Maastrichtian-age Upper Cretaceous rocks

facts.statement: The time range for Pabwehshi is estimated to be between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus is based on a partial snout and lower jaw elements, including a second snout assigned to the genus.
facts.quote: It is based on GSP-UM 2000, a partial snout and corresponding lower jaw elements, with another snout assigned to it.

facts.statement: Pabwehshi possessed serrated, interlocking teeth in its snout that created a zig-zag cutting edge.
facts.quote: Pabwehshi had serrated interlocking teeth in its snout that formed a "zig-zag" cutting edge.

facts.statement: Pabwehshi is an extinct genus of baurusuchine mesoeucrocodylian.
facts.quote: Pabwehshi (meaning "Pab [Formation] beast ["wehshi" in Urdu]") is an extinct genus of baurusuchine mesoeucrocodylian.

facts.statement: Larsson and Sues (2007) found a close affinity between Pabwehshi and the family Peirosauridae within Sebecia.
facts.quote: Larsson and Sues (2007) found close affinity between Pabwehshi and the Peirosauridae within Sebecia.

facts.statement: The parent group for Pabwehshi is Sebecosuchia.
The type species is P. pakistanensis, named in reference to Pakistan where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: The type species is P. pakistanensis, in reference to the nation where it was found.
